0x0f is the high byte of the 'syscall' instruction (0x0f 0x05); 0xcd is the opcode byte of 'int 0x80' (0xcd 0x80). The blacklist blocks both standard Linux syscall instruction encodings by forbidding their first/only opcode byte.
After blacklist passes, main() calls mprotect(buf, 0x64, PROT_READ|PROT_EXEC=4) changing the region from RWX to R-X (no longer writable)

Before jumping to shellcode, main() zeroes ALL general-purpose registers (rax,rbx,rcx,rdx,rsi,rdi,r8-r15), rsp, rbp, and all XMM registers (xmm0-xmm15). Then sets rdi=0x13370000 and executes 'jmp rdi'.
At shellcode entry: rdi=0x13370000 (shellcode base, a fixed absolute address), rsp=0 (no stack), all other GPRs=0, all XMMs=0. Shellcode must set up its own stack before using push/call.
init() sets stdin/stdout/stderr to unbuffered (setvbuf with mode _IONBF=2) and alarm(60) — process will receive SIGALRM after 60 seconds

Runtime probe: program prints 'Input your shellcode here (max: 100): ' then reads stdin; feeding 'AAAA' (passes blacklist since no 0x0f/0xcd) results in Segmentation fault (expected: AAAA is not valid executable code)

mmap hint address 0x13370000 is a fixed constant compiled into the binary (mov QWORD PTR [rbp-0x18], 0x13370000); it is not ASLR-randomized (MAP_FIXED not used but hint is specific; in practice kernel honors hint when available)

read() return value is stored in [rbp-0x1c] (int). If read returns 0 (EOF/empty), program aborts with 'read failed!'. Negative return (error) is NOT explicitly checked — it would be treated as nonzero and proceed (potential edge case for S2).
blacklist scans a fixed 100 bytes regardless of actual read length; bytes beyond read length are 0 (from memset), which pass the filter
GOT is in .got at 0x3f78 (size 0x88); Full RELRO means GOT is resolved at load time and made read-only — GOT overwrite is not viable

uncertainties.reason: Code checks 'cmp [rbp-0x1c], 0; jne' — a negative return would pass this check (nonzero) and proceed to blacklist/execute uninitialized-ish buffer. Edge case for S2.
